title: Russian forces withdraw from Snake Island
body:
On 30 June 2022 Russian forces withdrew from Snake Island, a small Ukrainian islet in the Black Sea that Russia had held since the early stages of the invasion. Russia's defence ministry called the withdrawal a "gesture of goodwill" after completing its tasks on the island. The move followed increased Ukrainian attacks on the outpost.

The ministry said the move was meant to show that Russia was not obstructing United Nations efforts to organise a humanitarian corridor for Ukrainian agricultural exports. It said the "ball is now in Ukraine's court" and blamed Ukraine for not clearing mines from its Black Sea coast. Moscow said the occupied port of Berdyansk had been demined and was ready to resume grain shipments.

Ukraine's commander-in-chief Valerii Zaluzhny hailed the withdrawal as a victory and thanked defenders of the Odesa region for liberating a strategically important part of the territory. Andriy Yermak, head of President Volodymyr Zelensky's office, said no Russian troops remained on the island. Ukraine and Western countries had accused Russia of blockading Ukrainian ports, which stalled grain exports. Russia and Ukraine together supply nearly a third of the world's wheat, and the UN estimated that up to 181 million people in 41 countries could face food crisis or famine without a solution.
